title: Dorothy Vaughan leads the West Area Computers
summary: In 1949 Vaughan became acting head of Langley's segregated West Area Computers, later NACA's first Black supervisor, and taught herself and her staff Fortran ahead of electronic computers.
why: Kept a segregated team at the front of aerospace computing.

notes.problem: Source: acting head from 1949, 'served for years in an acting role'; 'first Black supervisor at NACA', not 'first African-American woman supervisor at Langley' in 1949.

unsung.contribution: Led NACA's segregated West Area Computers and retrained her staff in Fortran programming.
unsung.recognition: She was honoured with the Congressional Gold Medal only posthumously, in 2019.
